proof_summary: Take \(m=39101\) and \(N=2\cdot100943\cdot3^{39101}-1\); a Brillhart–Lehmer–Selfridge \(N+1\) test with the Lucas sequence \(U_k(6,3)\) proves \(N\) prime, using the complete factorization \(N+1=2\cdot100943\cdot3^{39101}\). Modular exponentiation in \(\mathbb Z[\sqrt{24}]\) establishes \(N\mid U_{N+1}\) and \(\gcd(U_{(N+1)/q},N)=1\) for the only prime divisors \(q=2,3,100943\), so this positive exponent supplies the required counterexample.
